text:
Oliver: heads up — deploy-bot just put the staging canary on hold. runner OOM during artifact upload and cache lease never freed. blocking promote.
Deploy-bot: Promote paused: staging/canary failed (runner-37 OOM + cache-lease-stall). Auto-unhold: none. See logs.
Sarah: paste logs? is this the same cache leak we saw last month? :thinking_face: 
Ben: grabbing logs now. short snippet: 
```
[2026-03-22T10:12:03Z] runner-37 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 14233 (python) total-vm:1023456kB
[2026-03-22T10:12:05Z] uploader: multipart upload failed: timeout while completing parts
[2026-03-22T10:12:06Z] cache-manager: lease acquisition timeout=30s key=staging-artifact-abc123
```
Ben: looks like runner OOM triggered an incomplete multipart upload, leaving a stale cache lease. subsequent jobs hit lease and hang.
Mariela: ugh. that explains the long queue. runner memory spike correlates with a new test harness change (db-fixture parallelization).
Oliver: options: 1) pin to last-green artifact and manual promote now, 2) rollback runners to previous image that doesn't have the harness change, 3) try a targeted rerun of the single failing job after cleaning stale leases.
Sarah: i'd prefer targeted rerun + lease cleanup if fast. pinning blocks any config fixes. can we clean leases safely?
Ben: lease cleanup script exists: `scripts/ci/clean_stale_leases.sh --prefix=staging-`. i've run it in dev and it removes orphaned leases. cost is risking removing a currently-active lock if misused.
Oliver: marker: change window ends in ~2h. if targeted rerun clears canary in 10-15m we can promote. else we'll pin and manually promote to avoid delaying release.
Deploy-bot: CI hold created by deploy-bot at 1710900000 for staging/canary. Manual unhold allowed by release-eng or on successful canary.
CI-bot: kicking off `staging/canary` rerun for job #3421 (uploader+cache).
Sarah: also adding a short timeout on multipart completion in the job to reduce stray parts: set ENV UPLOAD_PART_TIMEOUT=20 (temporary). small patch pushed to canary config.
Ben: running lease cleanup now (`./scripts/ci/clean_stale_leases.sh --prefix=staging-`) — will report.
Ben: cleanup done, removed 3 leases, no active holders reported. re-run still in progress.
CI-bot: rerun complete: staging/canary #3421 -> failed (same OOM).
Mariela: if rerun still OOM, likely memory regression in runner image. we should rollback runner image to prior stable and rerun.
Oliver: agree. given rerun failed, we don't want to pin over a real regression. plan: rollback runner image for staging (nodepool-image:v2026-02-18) -> rerun single job. if passes, allow manual promote.
Sarah: can infra do an image rollback quickly? how long to spin new runners?
Mariela: rolling back image via nodepool takes ~4-6m to drain and replace, then jobs will pick up. I'll start now.
Mariela: nodepool update initiated.
Ben: requeued job after image rollback.
CI-bot: job #3421 requeued -> running on runner-42.
CI-bot: job #3421 -> success. artifacts uploaded and cache lease acquired+released cleanly.
Deploy-bot: staging/canary passed. Deploy-bot: manual promote available.
Oliver: decision: do not pin. we rolled back runner image (nodepool) and validated canary passed. Sarah, can you run manual promote when ready and add a short note to the release: "rolled back staging runner image to mitigate OOM during multipart uploads; no artifact changes"?
Sarah: yup. will promote and add release note. :white_check_mark: 
Ben: filing a follow-up issue to revert the test harness parallelization change and add more mem headroom on runners: ENG-RT-1429.
Oliver: thanks team. keeping the change window intact. closing thread after promote.
Sarah: promoted. release note: "staging: temporary runner image rollback to avoid multipart upload OOMs; follow-up to revert test harness change. See ENG-RT-1429."
Mariela: logging done. will monitor next 2 canaries. :eyes:
